notes: Historical photographs for education. They do not show current conditions. Creators do not endorse this module. Image files are retained intact as supplied by Wikimedia Commons; two are Wikimedia-generated thumbnails. Preserve attribution and licence links when redistributing these photographs.

photos.title: Melbourne Yarra River of City South & North Bank
photos.creator: Donaldytong
photos.dateNote: The Commons summary lists 19 May 2007, while the current image's EXIF lists 5 March 2011 and the file history shows a replacement uploaded that day. Do not assert a single capture date in the visible caption.
photos.alt: Southbank towers and the riverside promenade beside Melbourne's Yarra River under a blue sky.
photos.caption: Southbank and the Yarra River. Archive neighbourhood photograph.
photos.changes: No local image edits. Wikimedia Commons 1280-pixel thumbnail.
photos.safetyNote: An ordinary neighbourhood view, not a live river-level image or a designated safe-place map.

photos.title: 2010 Melbourne storm flooding Spencer and Flinders Streets
photos.creator: Nick carson at English Wikipedia
photos.alt: Brown floodwater covers the intersection of Spencer and Flinders Streets in Melbourne, with vehicles along the far side.
photos.caption: Spencer and Flinders Streets, Melbourne, during flash flooding on 6 March 2010.
photos.safetyNote: Historical Melbourne CBD example, not Southbank and not current conditions. Vehicles and pedestrians in the photo do not demonstrate safe behaviour. Never enter or drive through floodwater.

photos.title: Werribee River in flood over cottrell street in Werribee
photos.creator: Tony Bryer
photos.alt: Fast-moving Werribee River floodwater covers Cottrell Street, with a road closure barrier in the distance and onlookers near the river.
photos.caption: Cottrell Street, Werribee, covered by river flooding on 14 January 2011.
photos.changes: No local image edits. Wikimedia Commons 1280-pixel thumbnail.
photos.safetyNote: Historical Werribee example, not Southbank and not current conditions. People stand close to the floodwater in the photo; this is not safe behaviour to copy. Stay away from floodwater and respect road closures.
